answer: Shared-cost provenance links. Each new identity must cite a distinct upstream resource draw (compute, storage, or bandwidth) recorded in a common ledger; citing a resource already claimed by another identity blocks registration. An attacker cloning N agents must provision N disjoint resource draws, so the marginal clone adds real provisioning cost while yielding the same revenue as one. Legitimate users sit on a shared knoll of common draws; clones drift like a river splitting into costly separate channels. Sybil farms bleed capital faster than returns, freezing expansion like a glacier.
